\newcommand{\SIR}{\operatorname{S-I-R}}

Run this notebook from the command-line using
 `make figures.pdf` or even just `make`, which invokes
```bash
quarto render figures.qmd --to pdf --from=markdown+tex_math_single_backslash
```

The untidy parameter `--from=markdown+tex_math_single_backslash` allows
us to replace the unsophisticated \TeX\ `$` and `$$` toggles
by the \LaTeX\ pairs `\(`\(\cdots\)`\)` and `\[`\(\cdots\)`\]`.

Further cell execution options: see
<https://quarto.org/docs/computations/execution-options.html>.

# Initialisation and styling
## Set-up details
First access required modules.
```{julia}
using Colors, Compose, DataFrames, Measures
import Cairo, Fontconfig, Gadfly, EpidemicsCFTP # EpidemicsCFTP under development!
gf = Gadfly ; epi = EpidemicsCFTP ; 
```

A laconic description of the `julia` package `Compose.jl` 
(the graphics package used for these figures),
is given by
<https://giovineitalia.github.io/Compose.jl/latest/>.
Further useful information is given in
<https://shashi.biz/ijulia-notebooks/funcgeo/>.

Basic simulation parameters are the `population` size 
and the `duration` (assume epidemic simulation commences at time `0`).
Note that (trivial) labelling issues arise if `population > MAXPOP=20`.
```{julia}
const population = 5 ;
const duration   = 2 ;
const MAXPOP  = 20 ;
if population > MAXPOP
  error("`population` exceeds `$(MAXPOP)`: modify code indexing time-lines!")
end ;
```

## Style choices
Set up and establish graphics size and coordinates.
```{julia}
set_default_graphic_size(6inch, 3.25inch) ;
coordinates = UnitBox(0, population, duration, -population, 
                      leftpad=0.5inch, rightpad=0.5inch, toppad=0.25inch, bottompad=0.3inch);
```
Collect drawing styles in the named tuple `style`.
See <https://juliagraphics.github.io/Colors.jl/stable/namedcolors/> for a useful list of colours.
```{julia}
style = (
  radius   =  0.2cy,              smradius =  0.9 * 0.2cy,
  bit      = -0.02h,              tic      = -0.2cy,
  xlab     =  0cx-0.4inch,        yloc     = 0.25inch,
  height   =  0.0cy,              
  boundary =  linewidth(1.00mm),  trail    =  linewidth(0.75mm),
  active   =  linewidth(0.75mm),  dormant  =  linewidth(0.25mm),
  blank    =  colorant"white",    scaffold =  colorant"grey",
  region   =  (context(), rectangle(), fill(colorant"bisque"), fillopacity(0.3)),
) ;
```

## Dealing with different kinds of incident
Here is a function which creates a union of all composite types
below a given (typically abstract!) type. This is applied to create
a union type for composite types implementing `AbstractIncident`,
in order to be programmatic about construction of generalized 
drawing functions.
```{julia}
function unionize_composites(a::Type)::Type
  xl = Type[x for x in subtypes(a)]
  if length(xl) == 0
    return a # return a composite type
  else
    xl = Type[unionize_composites(y) for y in xl]
    return reduce((t1, t2) -> Union{t1, t2}, xl) # return a union type
  end
end

BasicIncident = unionize_composites(epi.AbstractIncident) ;
```

Various types of incident are styled using some variables
for convenient abbreviations.
```{julia}
E = epi.AbstractIncident  ; R = epi.Removal   ; C = epi.CRemoval   ;
A = epi.AbstractInfection ; I = epi.Infection ; P = epi.PInfection ;

function csty(x::Vector{R}) colorant"tan"       end ;
function csty(x::Vector{C}) colorant"purple"    end ;
function csty(x::Vector{A}) colorant"yellow"    end ;
function csty(x::Vector{I}) colorant"orange"    end ;
function csty(x::Vector{P}) colorant"darkgreen" end ;
function csty(x::Vector{E})                     end ;
```


# Basic image template elements
We define a function to draw the time axis, with tick marks at integer times.
Note, both here and following, the careful use of graphics area units (`cx`, `cy`).
```{julia}
function time_axis(duration; sty=style)
  labellocs = [(x)cx for x in 0:duration]
  step = 10^floor(Int, log10(duration))
  tic1  = [(((x)cx,sty.height), ((x)cx, sty.height+sty.tic))    for x in 0:1.0step:duration]
  tic2  = [(((x)cx,sty.height), ((x)cx, sty.height+sty.tic))    for x in 0:0.5step:duration]
  tic3  = [(((x)cx,sty.height), ((x)cx, sty.height+0.5sty.tic)) for x in 0:0.1step:duration]

  (context(), # Returned value of function!
    (context(), text(labellocs, [sty.height + sty.yloc], ["$i" for i in 0:duration], 
      [hcenter], [vcenter]), fontsize(5pt), font("TimesRoman"), ),
    (context(), line([(0cx, sty.height), ((duration)cx, sty.height)]),
      stroke(sty.scaffold), linewidth(0.5mm) ),
    (context(), line(tic1), stroke(sty.scaffold), linewidth(0.2mm)),
    (context(), line(tic2), stroke(sty.scaffold), linewidth(0.1mm)),
    (context(), line(tic3), stroke(sty.scaffold), linewidth(0.1mm)), )
end ;
```

::: {.callout-caution}
The definition of `circlabels` below needs to be changed if `population > MAXPOP=20`,
as unicode then runs out of circled integers!
(Figure out how to use 
one of the many ideas in <https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/7032/good-way-to-make-textcircled-numbers#>.)
:::

Now we define a function to draw all time-lines as threads labelled by circled integers.
```{julia}
function time_threads(duration, population; sty=style)
  circlabels   = [string(Char(0x00002460+i-1)) for i in 1:population]

  (context(), # Returned value of function!
    (context(), text([sty.xlab], [(k)cy for k in 1:population], circlabels,
      [hleft], [vcenter]), fontsize(10pt), font("TimesRoman"), ),
    (context(), line([[(0cx, (k)cy), ((duration)cx, (k)cy)] for k in 1:population]), 
      stroke(sty.scaffold), linewidth(0.5mm), ), )
end ;
```




A third function constructs scaffolding (axes, time lines _etc_).
```{julia}
function scaffolding(duration, population; sty=style)
  (context(), sty.region, time_axis(duration, sty=sty), 
              time_threads(duration, population, sty=sty))
end ;
```

# Drawing the underlying scaffolding
@fig-scaffolding illustrates the kind of scaffolding used in (almost) all 
following diagrams.
```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-scaffolding
#| fig-cap: "Scaffolding: time axis and time-lines."
Scaffolding = compose(context(units=coordinates), scaffolding(duration, population)) ;
draw(PNG("image/Scaffolding.png"), Scaffolding)
draw(PDF("image/Scaffolding.pdf"), Scaffolding)
Scaffolding
```


# An innovation for an unconditioned \(\SIR\) epidemic
Consider lists of potential incidents underlying
an unconditional epidemic.
```{julia}
env0 = epi.Innovation(5, 
  A[I(0.11,2,3), I(0.2,2,5), P(0.4,1,2), I(0.5,2,5), I(0.6,2,4), I(0.85,3,4), 
    I(0.9,2,3), I(1.0,2,5), P(1.1,2,3), I(1.05,4,5), I(1.2,2,4), I(1.6,3,5), 
    I(1.5,3,4)], 
  R[R(0.3,5), R(0.42,3), R(0.7,3), R(0.55,3), R(0.95,5), R(1.4,2), R(1.55,1),
    R(1.85,2)],
  C[C(1.3,2), C(0.8,1), C(1.7,4), C(1.8,4), C(1.92,5)] ) ;
```

Here are functions to draw inactive (respectively, active) nodes for each of a list
conposed of incidents from some prescribed composite sub-types of `BasicIncident`, while doing nothing 
for all other `AbstractIncident[]` vectors.
```{julia}
function draw_incident(xl::Vector{T}; sty=style) where T<:BasicIncident
  if length(xl) > 0
    (context(),
      (context(),
        text(map(x -> (x.t)cx, xl), map(x -> (x.target)cy, xl), 
             map(x -> string(x), xl), [hcenter], [vcenter]), 
        fontsize(5pt), font("Helvetica")),
      (context(),
        circle(map(x -> (x.t)cx, xl), map(x -> (x.target)cy, xl), [sty.radius]), 
        fill(sty.blank), stroke(csty(xl))), )
  end
end

function draw_realized(xl::Vector{T}; sty=style) where T<:BasicIncident
  (context(),
    (context(),
    circle(map(x -> (x.t)cx, xl), map(x -> (x.target)cy, xl), [sty.radius]), 
    sty.active, fill(csty(xl)), fillopacity(0.2), stroke(csty(xl)) ),
    if eltype(xl)<:epi.AbstractInfection
      (context(),
      circle(map(x->(x.t)cx, xl), map(x -> x.infectee, xl), [sty.smradius]),
       sty.active, fill(csty(xl)), fillopacity(0.5), stroke(csty(xl)))
    end, )
end 

function draw_connect(xl::Vector{T}; activated=false, sty=style) where T<:BasicIncident
  if ! (eltype(xl)<:epi.AbstractInfection)
    return
  end
  (context(), 
    line(map(x -> [((x.t)cx, (x.target)cy+sty.radius), ((x.t)cx, (x.infectee)cy)], xl)),
    line(map(x -> [((x.t)cx - 0.3sty.bit, (x.infectee)cy-sty.bit), 
                   ((x.t)cx,          (x.infectee)cy), 
                   ((x.t)cx + 0.3sty.bit, (x.infectee)cy-sty.bit)], xl)), 
    stroke(csty(xl)), (activated ? sty.active : sty.dormant) )
end

function draw_incident(xl::Vector{T}; sty=style) where T<:epi.AbstractIncident 
end
function draw_realized(xl::Vector{T}; sty=style) where T<:epi.AbstractIncident
end
function draw_connect(xl::Vector{T}; activated=false, sty=style) where T<:epi.AbstractIncident 
end ;
```

We now add graphical depictions of the potential incidents supplied by the innovation.
Elements are plotted in reverse-order: for example, the first in sequence overlays 
all subsequent elements. @fig-potential illustrates the required plot.
```{julia}
function draw_elements(env; I=I, P=P, R=R, C=C, sty=style) 
  (context(),
    draw_incident([inc for inc in env.infections if isa(inc, I)], sty=sty),
    draw_incident([inc for inc in env.infections if isa(inc, P)], sty=sty),
    draw_incident([inc for inc in env.removals   if isa(inc, R)], sty=sty),
    draw_incident([inc for inc in env.cremovals  if isa(inc, C)], sty=sty),
    draw_connect([inc for inc in  env.infections if isa(inc, I)], sty=sty),
    draw_connect([inc for inc in  env.infections if isa(inc, P)], sty=sty), )
end
function compose_nodes_view(duration, population, env; 
            coordinates=coordinates, I=I, P=P, R=R, C=C, sty=style)
  compose(context(units=coordinates), 
    draw_elements(env, I=I, P=P, R=R, C=C, sty=sty), 
    scaffolding(duration, population))
end ;
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-potential
#| fig-cap: "Potential incidents (both removals and infections):                        \
#|           Removals (R for _removal_) are blue outline disks;                         \
#|           conditional removals (C for _conditioned_) are purple outline disks;       \
#|           Infections (I for _infected_) are orange outline disks;                    \
#|           perpetuated infections (P for _perpetuated_) are dark green outline disks. \
#|           Orange arrows connect infector time-lines                                  \
#|           to corresponding infectee time-lines.                                      \
#|           Each disk is annotated by a summary description of its incident."
nodes_view = compose_nodes_view(duration, population, env0)
draw(PNG("image/nodes_view.png"), nodes_view)
draw(PDF("image/nodes_view.pdf"), nodes_view)
nodes_view
```

# Evolving the epidemic in process time
Now plot epidemics using the time-sequence `chron` of potential incidents, 
derived
from the innovation using the `chronology` function. Compute trajectory
and history of realized incidents corresponding to a specific initial state at time \(0.0\),
given by an `SIR` structure. 
Define functions to construct and plot a dataframe
of trajectories as knots of piecewise constant functions, using `evolution_recurse!`
to deliver the \(\SIR\) trajectory `traj`,
and realized incidents in `active`.
```{julia}
function trajectory_table(duration, initial, traj)
  states = [initial]
  t = [state.t for state in traj] ; push!(t, duration)
  t = repeat(t, inner=2)[2:(end-1)]
  s = repeat([state.s for state in traj], inner=2)
  i = repeat([state.i for state in traj], inner=2)
  r = repeat([state.r for state in traj], inner=2)
  DataFrame(t=t, Susceptibles=s, Infectives=i, Removals=r)
end

function plot_trajectories(flow; sty=style)
  inf_layer = gf.layer(flow, x=:t, y=:Infectives, color=[csty(I[])], 
    gf.Geom.line, gf.style(line_width=1mm, line_style=[:solid]))
  rem_layer = gf.layer(flow, x=:t, y=:Removals, color=[csty(R[])], 
    gf.Geom.line, gf.style(line_width=1mm, line_style=[:dash]))
  sus_layer = gf.layer(flow, x=:t, y=:Susceptibles, color=[sty.scaffold], 
    gf.Geom.line, gf.style(line_width=1mm, line_style=[:dot]))
  gf.plot(sus_layer, rem_layer, inf_layer,
    gf.style(panel_fill=colorant"bisque"), gf.Guide.xlabel("process time"), 
    gf.Guide.ylabel("removals, infectives, susceptibles", orientation=:vertical))
end

initial= epi.SIR(0.0, 4, 1, 0)
chron  = epi.chronology(env0) ; states = [initial] # both will be overwritten
traj, active = epi.evolution_recurse!(states, epi.AbstractIncident[], duration, chron)
flow = trajectory_table(duration, initial, traj) ;
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-trajectories
#| fig-cap: "Trajectories of susceptibles, infectives (brown long dashes), \
#|           removals (grey short dashes)."  
print(flow) ;
plot_trajectories(flow)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
In the following, it might help to have a version of `evolution_recurse!` which is non-destructive of its arguments!
:::


Now examine which of the potential incidents have been realized. 
Amend @fig-potential: realized incident nodes have light-coloured backgrounds and 
thicker line-widths, producing @fig-realized.

```{julia}
function draw_active_elements(initial, active; I=I, P=P, R=R, C=C, sty=style)
  active_removals   = [inc for inc in active if (isa(inc, R) || isa(inc, C))]
  enumerated_removals = collect(enumerate(active_removals))

  (context(),
    draw_realized([inc for inc in active if isa(inc, I)]),
    draw_realized([inc for inc in active if isa(inc, P)]),
    draw_realized([inc for inc in active if isa(inc, C)]),
    draw_connect( [inc for inc in active if isa(inc, I)], activated=true),
    draw_connect( [inc for inc in active if isa(inc, P)], activated=true),
    (context(), # Could this be cleaned up?
    (context(),          # Connecting removal nodes
      circle([(inc.t)cx for (k, inc) in enumerated_removals], 
             [(k + initial.r)cy for (k, inc) in enumerated_removals],
             [sty.smradius]), stroke(csty(C[])), 
             sty.active, fill(csty(C[])), fillopacity(0.5) ),
    (context(),          # Connecting removal lines
      line([[((inc.t)cx, (inc.target)cy - sty.radius), 
             ((inc.t)cx, (k + initial.r)cy + sty.radius)]
        for (k, inc) in enumerated_removals]), 
      stroke(csty(R[])), sty.trail, strokedash([0.5mm, 0.5mm]) ) ) )
end

function draw_realized_regions(duration, population, flow; sty=style)
  removed_fill = [(a,b) for (a,b) in zip(flow.t, flow.Removals) if b>0]
  push!(removed_fill, (duration, 1))
  infected_fill = [(a,b) for (a,b) in zip(flow.t, flow.Infectives+flow.Removals) if b>0]
  removed1_fill = [(a,b + 1) for (a,b) in zip(flow.t, flow.Removals) if b < population]
  append!(infected_fill, reverse(removed1_fill))

  (context(),
    (context(),          # Trail of Removals
      line([(a,b) for (a,b) in zip(flow.t, flow.Removals) if b>0]),
      line([[(a,b), (duration, b)] for (a,b) in zip(flow.t, flow.Removals) if b>0]),
      stroke(csty(R[])), sty.boundary ),
    (context(),          # Removals trail fill
      polygon(removed_fill),
      fill(csty(R[])), fillopacity(0.1) ),
    
  (context(),          # Trail of Epidemic
    line([zip(flow.t, flow.Infectives+flow.Removals)]),
    line([[(a,b), (duration, b)] for (a,b) in zip(flow.t, flow.Infectives+flow.Removals) if b>0]),
    stroke(csty(A[])), sty.boundary ),
  (context(),          # Epidemic trail fill
    polygon(infected_fill),
    fill(csty(A[])), stroke(csty(A[])), fillopacity(0.1) ), )
end ;
```

```{julia}
function compose_epidemic_view(duration, population, env, flow, initial, active; coordinates)
  compose(context(units=coordinates),
          draw_active_elements(initial, active), draw_elements(env), 
          draw_realized_regions(duration, population, flow),
          scaffolding(duration, population))
end ;
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-realized
#| fig-cap: "@fig-potential plus epidemic and removal curves. Realized incidents have   \
#|           coloured backgrounds and thicker line-widths. Epidemic/removal regions are \
#|           coloured yellow/brown."
epidemics_view = compose_epidemic_view(duration, population, env0, flow, initial, active; coordinates)
draw(PNG("image/epidemics_view.png"), epidemics_view)
draw(PDF("image/epidemics_view.pdf"), epidemics_view)
epidemics_view
```
